answer:
**Desidae – Genus _Desis_ species that are each listed by the World Spider Catalog (WSC) as occurring in only a single country**

| Full scientific name | Indigenous country (or territory) | WSC reference |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------|----------------|
| *Desis bobmarleyi* Baehr, Raven & Harms, 2017 | Australia (Queensland) | [bobmarleyi](https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/62701) |
| *Desis gardineri* Pocock, 1904 | India (Laccadive Islands) | [gardineri](https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/15337) |
| *Desis inermis* Gravely, 1927 | India | [inermis](https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/15339) |
| *Desis japonica* Yaginuma, 1956 | Japan | [japonica](https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/15340) |
| *Desis jiaxiangi* Lin, Li & Chen, 2020 | China | [jiaxiangi](https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/64491) |
| *Desis kenyonae* Pocock, 1902 | Australia (Victoria, Tasmania) | [kenyonae](https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/15341) |
| *Desis risbeci* Berland, 1931 | New Caledonia | [risbeci](https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/15345) |
| *Desis vorax* L. Koch, 1872 | Samoa | [vorax](https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/15347) |

**Explanation**

The WSC lists each of these *Desis* species with a single country (or a single political territory) in the “Distribution” field.  None of the other accepted _Desis_ species in the WSC catalogue have distributions that are confined to a single country; they are either multi‑country or regionally broad (e.g., *Desis crosslandi* – Tanzania, Madagascar, Comoros, Mayotte; *Desis marina* – New Caledonia, New Zealand, etc.).  Therefore, the eight species above are the only members of the family Desidae, genus _Desis_, that are recorded by the World Spider Catalog as native to exactly one country.

**Desidae – Genus _Desis_ species that are each listed by the World Spider Catalog (WSC) as occurring in only a single country**

| Full scientific name | Indigenous country (or territory) | WSC reference |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------|----------------|
| *Desis bobmarleyi* Baehr, Raven & Harms, 2017 | Australia (Queensland) | [bobmarleyi](https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/62701) |
| *Desis gardineri* Pocock, 1904 | India (Laccadive Islands) | [gardineri](https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/15337) |
| *Desis inermis* Gravely, 1927 | India | [inermis](https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/15339) |
| *Desis japonica* Yaginuma, 1956 | Japan | [japonica](https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/15340) |
| *Desis jiaxiangi* Lin, Li & Chen, 2020 | China | [jiaxiangi](https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/64491) |
| *Desis kenyonae* Pocock, 1902 | Australia (Victoria, Tasmania) | [kenyonae](https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/15341) |
| *Desis risbeci* Berland, 1931 | New Caledonia | [risbeci](https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/15345) |
| *Desis vorax* L. Koch, 1872 | Samoa | [vorax](https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/15347) |

**Explanation**

The WSC lists each of these *Desis* species with a single country (or a single political territory) in the “Distribution” field.  None of the other accepted _Desis_ species in the WSC catalogue have distributions that are confined to a single country; they are either multi‑country or regionally broad (e.g., *Desis crosslandi* – Tanzania, Madagascar, Comoros, Mayotte; *Desis marina* – New Caledonia, New Zealand, etc.).  Therefore, the eight species above are the only members of the family Desidae, genus _Desis_, that are recorded by the World Spider Catalog as native to exactly one country.
